shots.title: Leaving orbit — secured inside the escape pod
shots.prompt:
Eight seconds, one continuous interior shot. Camera remains inside the compact escape cabin with a small smooth, purposeful lateral drift from Harper toward the side viewport. First about 3.5 seconds: Harper is already seated in the fixed cushioned chair, held by ordinary padded flight shoulder restraints; quiet breathing and a brief alert glance toward the window, hands below frame. Cabin structure and harness stay fixed. At about 3.5 seconds the cradle releases with one small believable inertial settling of her shoulders, without shake or violent recoil. The external graphite mother-ship hull, cyan gallery and docking lip begin sliding and receding across the side viewport as the capsule moves away. By about 5.7 seconds much more open starfield is visible and the mother ship is distinctly farther away. Keep the glass, ivory cabin, silver halter top, face and hairstyle unchanged. No lip-sync, strap fastening, finger gestures, suit change, tank, robots, interior transformation, cut, dissolve, zoom blur, audio or readable text. Release occurs during Leaving orbit in the planned edit, not before the interior is established.

shots.title: Clear, bank and accelerate
shots.prompt:
Six seconds, one continuous exterior shot. Start with the compact ovoid capsule already safely separated from the original massive graphite robot laboratory ship, as in the first frame. During the first 1.5 seconds extend the clearance gap smoothly along its present outward heading. Between roughly 1.5 and 3 seconds the pod performs one brisk, smooth bank with a small roll: its nose swings upward-right into open space, then the roll settles. From about 3 seconds accelerate decisively along that new upward-right arc, with restrained speed blur and a smooth camera follow that keeps the pod legible and lets the mother ship recede. The functional thin cyan-white ejection wake connects the initial departure direction to the release recess at first; as the heading changes, new wake follows the curved flight path. Brightest near the pod, the trail decays rapidly behind it into a long faint tail; it never becomes a tether, laser, solid line or spaghetti. Keep one pod, one unchanged mother ship, consistent hull proportions and coherent viewport/hatch/recessed drives.
